papers.title: Minimal Recurrent Behavioral Memory for Imitation under Partial Observability
papers.abstract: What is the least recurrent memory needed to reproduce a specified expert under partial observability? The instantaneous requirement is the conditional entropy of the expert's behavioral quotient, but recurrence must also preserve distinctions that future observations will not restore before use. We characterize this minimal recurrent behavioral memory by a compatibility relation: under transitivity its classes attain the exact minimum, while the general case is an entropy minimization over closed compatible state assignments, with exact certificates on finite instances. A sole-carrier measurement protocol separates behavioral sufficiency, excess code rate, and information carried by observations or other memory paths; experimental bit requirements refer to the induced symbolic behavioral model under the stated occupancy. Across manipulation tasks, learned code rates remain near zero- and two-bit requirements as hidden modes grow to $512$, and anticipatory memory follows a $2\to1\to0$ requirement despite zero instantaneous demand during waiting. Learning this representation remains difficult: event-agnostic future-behavior supervision yields $36/40$ sufficient seeds with one frozen configuration and improves the longest-horizon pixel setting from $0/8$ to $6/8$ sufficient held-out seeds (closed-loop success from $0.08$ to $0.57$). On unmodified community benchmarks, the protocol certifies delay-independent requirements, which sufficient codes match at mid-delay. The supervision aids commitment but can induce predictive surplus; annealing it lets imitation and rate training reduce that surplus, separating the information-theoretic target from the ability to learn it.

papers.title: Higher-Order Approximation of Exit Functionals in Sampling-Based Stochastic Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: Safety evaluation in sampling-based stochastic model predictive control often requires numerical estimation of exit functionals. The approximation of first-exit times and exit indicators is therefore a key numerical bottleneck, and discretization error in these quantities directly affects the resulting controller. This paper studies how existing higher-order methods for strong approximation of exit times can be brought into safe control. Two cases are highlighted. For general noncommutative dynamics, an adaptive order-1 Milstein discretization is used together with Lévy-area simulation via Wiktorsson's method. For commutative dynamics, an adaptive order-1.5 construction achieves a stronger exit-time rate. Under a local anti-concentration condition on the exit-time law, we show that strong exit-time approximation transfers to strong approximation of the failure indicator. The methods are then studied in the context of chance-constrained path integral control, which provides an exact continuous-time representation of safety through exit events. Numerical experiments compare the two cases in terms of strong exit-time error, failure-indicator error, and closed-loop constraint satisfaction, showing improvement over Euler-Maruyama and thereby enabling existing and future techniques whose applicability depends on improved strong approximation.

executive_summary: CMU introduces JAMB, a joint action–motion diffusion policy that substantially boosts success and robustness in bimanual manipulation.
New motion-planning and control methods advance constrained planning, dynamic deformable-object manipulation, and humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation.
Multiple works push dexterous and forceful manipulation forward, from all-linear Cartesian fingers and visually grounded fingertip forces to tool-use via hand–object mechanisms.
Navigation and SLAM see progress in prediction-aware legged obstacle avoidance, monocular and drone navigation, semantic orchard mapping, and radar–lidar SE(3) localization.
Vision-language(-action) systems continue to mature, with geometry-aware and safety-wrapped VLA manipulation, sparse semantic navigation, and unified embodied models.

UC San Diego, UC Berkeley, and Stanford contribute institution-aligned work spanning continuum catheter localization, free-flyer space manipulation, driving-safety benchmarking, and humanoid-RL education.

institution_matches.title: JAMB: Joint Action-Motion Diffusion for Bimanual Manipulation
institution_matches.overview: JAMB jointly denoises bimanual actions and future 3D point tracks in a shared transformer, explicitly coupling control and predicted scene geometry. On 16 simulated tasks and several real-robot evaluations, it strongly outperforms action-only and auxiliary-geometry baselines, with better generalization in cluttered and out-of-distribution scenes.

institution_matches.title: Shaft-Configuration-Adaptive Catheter Tip Position Estimation via Motor-History Conditioned Residual Learning
institution_matches.overview: This work augments a calibrated geometric catheter model with a motor-history-conditioned GRU residual corrector to estimate 3D tip pose without explicit shaft sensing. Across multiple catheters and bent configurations, it cuts tip-position error by ~59% versus a constant-curvature baseline, improving navigation accuracy for tendon-driven continuum instruments.

institution_matches.title: A Deployable Four-Finger Payload for Teleoperated Free-Flying Manipulation with Astrobee
institution_matches.overview: The authors design a 17-DoF, four-finger payload on a linear rail for NASA’s Astrobee, controlled via VR teleoperation to map human hand motions to bimanual free-flyer manipulation. Zero-gravity MuJoCo simulations on cargo transport tasks show feasible performance and quantify success, contact maintenance, and task times.

institution_matches.title: NavSafe-$\infty$: Benchmarking Closed-Loop Driving Safety in Photorealistic Environments
institution_matches.overview: NavSafe-$\infty$ is a photorealistic closed-loop benchmark of 280 driving scenarios with safety-centric taxonomies for crashes, violations, and incidents. Evaluating 20 end-to-end policies reveals weak correlation between open-loop metrics and closed-loop safety, and shows how common training remedies can trade safety margin for progress.

institution_matches.title: Teaching Reinforcement Learning and Humanoid Robotics to High-School Students: An Expert-Validated Curriculum Design on a Low-Cost Open Platform
institution_matches.overview: This paper proposes a research-inspired curriculum where high-school students assemble an open-source humanoid, train a walking policy in simulation, and deploy it on hardware. Expert review surfaces key design tensions—authenticity vs. cognitive load, integration vs. visible progress, and teamwork vs. accountability—informing a reusable framework for precollege robotics courses.

topic_matches.title: Induced Riemannian Metrics for Motion Planning with Constraints
topic_matches.overview: The authors formalize motion planning on constraint submanifolds using induced Riemannian metrics, ensuring that implicit and explicit task-space representations share the same geometry. They extend both sampling-based planning and trajectory optimization under general metrics, and demonstrate benefits on constrained bimanual manipulation with dual Franka arms.

topic_matches.title: PLAT: Sparse Timed Keyframe Motion Tracking for Humanoid Control via Privileged Latent Transition Learning
topic_matches.overview: PLAT learns humanoid controllers that track sparse future keyframes with timing rather than dense motion, using privileged dense motion during training to shape a latent transition model. A latent residual RL stage refines transitions instead of raw actions, yielding stable, accurate whole-body motions in simulation and on a Unitree G1.

topic_matches.title: HOTICE: Whole-Body Humanoid Object Transportation in Cluttered Environments
topic_matches.overview: HOTICE combines humanoid–object decoupled potential fields with a dual-agent RL architecture that separates upper- and lower-body control while sharing state and rewards. Trained via specialist-to-generalist distillation, the policy enables a Unitree G1 to transport varied objects through clutter with coordinated whole-body collision avoidance.

topic_matches.title: Brace Yourself: Task-Conditioned Environmental Bracing for Forceful Humanoid Manipulation
topic_matches.overview: This work introduces Supporting Hand Strategy (SHS), which learns to use one arm to brace against the environment while the other performs forceful tasks. On a Unitree G1, SHS boosts sustainable interaction forces from 13.5 N to about 60 N and improves force tracking, extending humanoid manipulation capability without online trajectory optimization.

topic_matches.title: VisForce: Visual Grounding of Current and Desired Forces for Goal-Conditioned Dexterous Manipulation
topic_matches.overview: VisForce encodes current and desired fingertip forces as rendered visual cues over wrist and goal images, then uses cross-attention to produce force-aware actions. On a UR10 with a dexterous hand, it achieves consistent force-conditioned grasps and 40–70% success on multi-stage force-sensitive tasks such as slip-modulated peg-in-hole.

topic_matches.title: The Cartesian Hand: In-Hand Manipulation with All-Linear Fingers
topic_matches.overview: The Cartesian Hand is a 7-DoF end-effector with two independent parallel grippers and four translating fingertips that generate relative object motion using only linear DOFs. Its configuration-independent fingertip kinematics enable complex in-hand tasks—threaded closures, pipetting, triggers, screwdriving—on 35 objects, including bimanual use on a humanoid.

topic_matches.title: Relative Contact Velocity-Controlled Hand-Object Mechanism for Dexterous Tool Manipulation
topic_matches.overview: This paper models a hand and tool as a unified hand–object mechanism controlled via Cartesian relative contact velocities and forces between generalized contact frames. A lightweight least-squares motion planner and complementary filter enable five different multi-finger hands to execute full tool-use sequences—grasp, reorient, and wield—from the same simple references.

topic_matches.title: CableVLA: Simulation-Privileged Global-Local Representation Learning for Cable Routing
topic_matches.overview: CableVLA couples a topology-aware visual head (TopoHead) with a tactile encoder (TacSense) to learn global cable configuration and local contact dynamics from simulation-privileged signals. A contact gate injects force-tactile residuals into a frozen policy, raising simulated cable-routing success from ~63% to ~85% and improving slip detection versus CNN-LSTM baselines.

topic_matches.title: Manipulation of Deformable Linear Objects Using Model Predictive Path Integral Control with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Learning
topic_matches.overview: The authors learn DLO dynamics with a biLSTM trained on MuJoCo data and embed it in a Model Predictive Path Integral controller for closed-loop cable-like object manipulation. Simulations and experiments show accurate trajectory tracking and efficient control despite the object’s high-dimensional, nonlinear behavior.

topic_matches.title: Manipulation with Stability Guarantees: Linear Deformable Objects with Non-negligible Physical Response Grasped at Multiple Location
topic_matches.overview: This work develops a fully dynamic model of linear deformable objects with multiple actuation points and recasts manipulation as shape regulation via forces and torques in SE(3). Nonlinear feedback laws provide explicit steady-state convergence conditions, and simulations plus real-time experiments with online shape estimation demonstrate stable manipulation beyond quasi-static regimes.
